Over the last few years we of the Marconi Club have enjoyed to the full sailing from a site which must be considered one of the best in Essex.

Unfortunately during this time we have not been able to enjoy a sense of security. There has always been doubt in our minds as to how long we shall be sailing from Stansgate. In spite of the efforts of Officers past and present in 1968, and although we were still at Stansgate; we could not boast of security of tenure,

During the latter half of 1968 your Vice Commodore, Stan Allerton, and

behalf of the club. It was quite a comprehensive development involving some ? I spent some considerable time in preparing a plan to develop Stansgate on /

three acres, with a new Club House and anciilary buildings with maps, detailed drawi’ gs and costing and above all details of justification. The scheme involved the purchase of three acres of land or a long term lease of no less than 21 years with a built-in incentive for our landlord.

On the following Sunday Stan and I met Pat. Sparrow to present our proposals, but before we could do so were informed by Mr. Sparrow that he was negotiating the sale of his two farms to Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge and that a draft contract was in the process of being drawn up. Should we therefore wishto discuss an extension of our lease, we had best contact their Agent, Mr. Stafford Smith. To say the least, Stan and I came away somewhat dejected.

On December 14th, 1968 I again went to see Mr. Sparrow and was introduced to Mr. Stafford Smith who went into great detail to outline a development scheme he had in mind for Stansgate. I do not propose to go into detail of this very ambitious scheme, but as I alone could not commit either the club or the Company (who were being asked to get involved), I suggested that I convene a meeting between Company Representatives, Mr. Stafford Smith and
myself.

At this stage I was offered the services of Mr. Riddel, the Company Property Of:icer, as a legal representative who was briefed on all aspects, including the past history of the club.

To sum up, the results of the meeting with Mr. Stafford-Smith
were
negative since he was not in a position to commit himself eat this stage.

The contract of the sale of the farms was signed in March,
1969.
Mr. Riddel and I have met Mr. Stefford-Smith on two occasions since and we have a very good understanding; he is aware of our requirements and we have reason to believe we know of his. He has not, as yet, had much Success with the development, but the scheme he has in mind will take time to progress,

Both Mr. Riddel and I are of the same mind that eventually the
situation
will resolve itself and that we, the Marconi i Sailing Club, will one day have the security we have been seeking over the years.

What of the future, assuming we are successful in our endeavours.
We may one day still have the opportunity to purchase or have a long lease. Should this come about, we shall have to have a development scheme of our
own
to include a larger Club House with better facilities. This, of course, will cost money and as our main source of income is subscriptions, it is inevitable that we shall have to dig deeper into our pockets.

This has been my last year in office - not a particularly fruitful year,
frustrating, in fact. I would, however, like to thank the Officers and Committee who have supported me over the past three years. -I would also like to thank all the members who have given their time, labour and donations to the various appezls I have made.

The ladies of the Club, as always, have given me their support.
Margaret Cottam who organised the Galley services, Ann Smith on social
work,
Joyce Polley for helping David our Treasurer. There are many others of course, but I must mention my wife Connie who has been very tolerant and helpful over the years, especially at times when club work came before the home.

Two ladies who need special mention are Avril Stevens «ss Social Secretary and Eleanor Witter, the Editor of Navigans. They have both done trojan work for the Club and their services, I am sure, are appreciated by all Club members,

I would like to close by wishing your new Officers and Committee Success in the future, and may the Club achieve the security it has earned Over the past fifteen years,

SAILING SECRETARY'S REPORT 1969

From the sailing point of view I feel 1969 will go down as a very good year. Average entries for points races have gone up, in some cases by an exceptional amount. Individual attempts at Open Meetings and Class Championships have also met with great success.

The reorganised Helmsman of the Year series has returned an average entry of 15 which is an increase of 25 on last year's figure. The total entry was 127 and suggests that the right formula has now been found.

The three main fleets have been consistent and in most cases have attracted more entries than last year. This is particularly true of the Enterprise Fleet whose average entry is up 80% on last year.

The three disappointments this year I think have been firstly, the non- emergence of the Mirror fleet which was mainly due to the discontinuity caused by the resignations of two fleet captains during the year, secondly the failure of the Handicap fleet to stage any race this year, and thirdly the failure of the Barnacle Points Series for cruisers. The Silhouette Cup run by us this year attracted only three entries too.

This year five new points series were introduced. The Spring Points series for GPl4s, Enterprises, Mirrors and Handicap Fleets and the Saturday Points series. Once again with the exceptions of the Mirror and Handicap

fleets, these proved satisfactory and- we hope n next year. to stage them agai
The three pursuit races this year proved to be popular once mid week races. more as were the

The
Regatta this year was extremely successful and I believe is fast becoming the big attraction of the year on the Blackwater. At this point I would like to thank John and Elesnor Witter for their invaluable help .in looking after the Regatta and somehow managing to get everything running so
smoothly.

The Challenge Cup this year attracted 51 entries as opposed to 30 last year, an increase of 70%.

Team racing has not been one of our stronger points this year, although we must congratulate the Hornet team for winning their team race versus Salcote S.C., the GP.14 team for bringing the Lawson and Cuthbert Cup home for their defeat of M.Y.C. and also the team skippered by Julian Bigden which achieved second place overall in the John Lewis Partnership team race event at Poole.

This year the greatest individual success has been achieved by Simon Darney who came second in the Hornet Nationals at Herne Bay and well up in the field at the World Championships at Hayling Island.

The rescue launches eve been far more reliable this year and I think this is due to the amount of work put in on the boats by the Bosun Ron Greygoose and Bill Mortimer, the Coxon, and I would like to express nay thanks to both of them and to Brian Urry who has helped Bill out on many an occasion. We have found, though, tht we still have not got enough coxons to even out 'the load' sufficiently and so next year the Race Organiser will be asked to provide a coxon as well as a Hace Officer. This idea of a Race Organiser has incidentally proved most satisfactory and we hope to carry it
through
to next year.

The race marks have stood up to a lot this year - certainly more boats
going round them, and my thanks go to Chris Cooper who has been looking after them this year.

I would also like to thank Nick Tovey for his work on the racing programme, especially as the time for its preparation comes round once more.

Looking forward to next year, we have been lucky enough to have been asked to stage the Enterprise East Cosst Area Championships at Stansgate which will I'm sure be the success that is becoming a frequent visitor to the Marconi Sailing Club.

Peter Crick

LADY ANNE'S SUMMER CRUISE 1969

Lady Anne is an eight ton auxiliary cutter. She was designed and built near Burnham
in 19355, and was owned by my father for right years from 1947-1955. She is a reomy boat, shoal draught, centreboard, not too good to windward in a short sea, but very strong and sound. We have every confidence in her,

The crew were to consist of myself, Frances, our two children, Fiona (4 years) and Nigel (24 years) and Trixie our black and tan terrier.

During
my father's ownership Lady Anne had been cruised in the Isle of Wight area, and I longed to take her back there. When my younger brother and his wife purchased a 45 ton cruiser last winter, we arranged to meet at Newtown Creek on the Isle of Wight. He keeps 'Freedom' at’ Weymouth, 60 miles west of I. of W. and we keep Lady Anne on the Blackwater in Hssex 150 miles east of I. of W. His holiday was limited to a fortnight, whereas we had a month.

Detailed plans were not made, as I wanted to keep time in hand to prevent my having to give the crew a hard bashing ut sea just to maintain a tight schedule. Broadly the plan was a week to I. of W., two weeks

ENTERPRISE NEWS

The Enterprise fleet held its Fleet Meeting on Friday 28th November, Twenty two helmsmen and crew came along and njoyed an interesting evening discussing developments within the Class and the coming season.

The main Class developments are that the Enterprise is about to become the International Enterprise and glass reinforced plastic hulls with wooden decks are to be allowed. Spinnakers are under consideration but are very
unlikely to be used next season.

The fleet remains very keen and we hope to have twelve or more boats out for each of the Enterprise Points rccs next yar. Some members of the fleet are already fitting out their boats for next season. One helmsman has completely stripped his hull and is now fitting new decks, others are waiting to receive new boats, sails, spars etc. for the coming season.

On a business note, the Club has held an Enterprise mast for use by fleet members for the last few years. This scheme was started as the delivery
of a new wooden mast was 6 - 8 weeks at one time. However, due to the fact
that a mast can usually be obtained ‘off the shelf' these days and some people prefer metal masts, it was decided at the meeting that this scheme should be
terminated.
